newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Martinair S African landing rights better.
newsitem.headline: Martinair S African landing rights better.

text.p: Martinair, the Dutch cargo and charter airline, has gained permanent rights to fly to South Africa, a company statement said.
The carrier has gained freight traffic rights under an NV-4 permit, which enables it to operate a twice-weekly service to South Africa.
Traffic rights to Johannesburg, Cape Town and Durban have now been granted. There is also the possibility of being able to carry out extra flights in the peak season.

Previously, Martinair had been granted an NV-3 permit but this had restrictions concerning the movement of perishable carg in that whatever volume of cargo was carried into South Africa, the carrier was forced to carry 90 percent perishable traffic when leaving. The NV-3 also meant that the carrier could not fly more than 52 flights a year.

Martinair, which is jointly owned by KLM and transport group, Nedlloyd, gained traffic rights under the NV-3 permit at the beginning of August. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
